operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names: 'advisedBy', 'taughtBy' (camelCase) alongside lowercase 'course','person'; must double-quote in generated SQL.

advisedBy has a composite PK (p_id, p_id_dummy) AND a composite FK (p_id,p_id_dummy)->person(p_id,p_id) — the FK parent column list repeats p_id, so the FK is effectively (p_id,p_id_dummy)->(person.p_id, person.p_id); parent column 'p_id' is used twice.
advisedBy.p_id_dummy is a FK to person.p_id but is also a PK member; its distinct count (39) is far below person.p_id distinct (278) — FK values are a strict subset, not a permutation.
taughtBy.p_id samples include 279 and 415 which exceed person.p_id max (person has 278 rows, p_id samples 3..7) — FK values may reference non-existent parents in the original (dangling FK rows).
taughtBy.course_id distinct 113 < course.course_id distinct 132 — FK subset again; also taughtBy has 189 rows > 132 courses, so course_id repeats (many-to-one).
All columns notnull=0 (nullable) even PKs; no NOT NULL constraints declared — TS will not be forced to emit non-null.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs; 'checked' flag will be false for all columns.
person.professor and person.student are INTEGER with only 2 distinct values (0/1) — boolean-like stored as int, TS Number fuzzer will produce wide ints, not 0/1.

person.hasPosition / inPhase / yearsInProgram are TEXT but store enum-like tokens ('Faculty','Faculty_adj','Post_Quals','Year_2',...) plus '0' — String fuzzer will emit random charset strings, not these tokens.
course.courseLevel TEXT with 3 distinct 'Level_300/400/500' — enum-like text.
All declared types are INTEGER or TEXT; no Date/Time/Bool/Bit/Year dispatch — every column goes to Number or String fuzzer.
Small tables (132/278/113/189 rows) — no huge-table sampling concern; original_values fully readable.
operator_ts_expectations: course_id, p_id, professor, student, p_id_dummy: Number fuzzer, scale from 'INTEGER' (no args -> scale 0, is_int True), range [-1,1] perturbed by +-1/+-2 — will produce tiny ints, mostly 0/1/-1, far from original 0..278.

courseLevel, hasPosition, inPhase, yearsInProgram: String fuzzer, length default 20, random charset a-zA-Z0-9() — will NOT reproduce 'Level_500','Faculty_adj','Year_10' tokens; FN risk on queries filtering these enums.

PK columns (course_id, p_id, composite PKs) get max_l0=inf (single) or 30 (composite) — fresh draws not capped, so PKs spread but Number range [-1,1] means heavy collisions -> sample_fresh_primary_keys drops many rows, shrinking tables below original sizes.

FK fill: advisedBy.p_id and p_id_dummy both drawn from person.p_id final values; taughtBy.course_id from course.course_id, taughtBy.p_id from person.p_id — consistent, but parent tables already shrunk by PK dedup, so FK cardinality collapses.
Composite PK (p_id,p_id_dummy) in advisedBy: both drawn independently from person.p_id, so many duplicate pairs -> heavy dedup, advisedBy may end up tiny.

Enum text columns: literal pool from train SQL may inject 'Faculty','Post_Quals' etc. as elements (p=0.2 fresh), giving partial coverage — but 80% fresh random strings break enum equality/IN filters -> FN.
Number fuzzer on professor/student (0/1) will emit values outside {0,1} -> queries like 'professor=1' may match wrong rows or none -> FP/FN.
No Date/Time columns, so no date-template quirks; no Bool/Bit dispatch.

Missing ties/duplicates: original has many-to-one (taughtBy 189 rows/113 courses, advisedBy 113/91 p_id) — TS dedup on PKs and unique columns may remove the duplicate multiplicity that aggregate queries (COUNT, GROUP BY) rely on -> FP on count-based gold.
Dangling FK in original (taughtBy.p_id=279,415) means original itself has rows with no parent; TS FK fill from parent values will NOT reproduce these -> queries relying on orphan rows differ.
String fuzzer contaminate (0.5) adds/removes chars -> enum tokens like 'Faculty' become 'FacultyX' etc., breaking exact-match filters.
